command:
set -eo pipefail
cd /tmp
echo "== verify the staged nanopore run against its pinned sha256 =="
printf '%s  %s\n' b9c7754312707051ee71f72c54feb10f19a0ee6a2f73ec6de20fb60cd8bb5ae4 ERR10114907.fastq.gz > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256
df -m /tmp | awk 'NR==2{print "tmpfs_total_mb "$2}'
( MAX=0; MEM=0; while :; do U=$(df -m /tmp | awk 'NR==2{print $3}')
    [ "$U" -gt "$MAX" ] && { MAX=$U; echo "$MAX" > /tmp/.peak; }
    # Flye's own footprint, not the staging area: tmpfs peaked at 769 MB on the first run,
    # so RAM is set by the assembler's working set and needs its own measurement before the
    # box can be sized down.
    M=$(awk '/MemTotal/{t=$2} /MemAvailable/{a=$2} END{printf "%.0f", (t-a)/1024}' /proc/meminfo)
    [ "$M" -gt "$MEM" ] && { MEM=$M; echo "$MEM" > /tmp/.mem; }
    sleep 5; done ) & SAMPLER=$!

echo "== flye --nano-hq: a real MinION run of E. coli, ~65x =="
# --nano-hq, not --nano-raw / --nano-corr: measured elsewhere in this catalog, Flye's raw
# modes OOM on inputs where --nano-hq fits.
# -t 8 is what a reader actually runs. Flye's thread count changes WHICH assembly the search
# lands on, so the exact contig count is NOT asserted below -- only properties any correct
# assembly of this organism must have. -t 1 is the byte-reproducible setting if you need one.
T0=$(date +%s)
flye --nano-hq ERR10114907.fastq.gz -g 4.6m -t 8 -o out > flye.log 2>&1
T1=$(date +%s); WALL=$(( T1 - T0 ))
kill "$SAMPLER" 2>/dev/null || true
PEAK=$(cat /tmp/.peak 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
RSS=$(cat /tmp/.mem 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
cp out/assembly.fasta assembly.fasta
cp out/assembly_info.txt assembly_info.txt
# Never rm a staged input: sticky /tmp, stage-in ran as the instance user, EPERM is not
# suppressed by `rm -f` and would kill the task under set -e.

# THE SENTINEL IS "Final assembly:", NOT "Done!". Both strings exist in Flye 2.9.6, but
# main.py:443's "Done!" is inside the standalone flye-polish path, which this invocation never
# takes -- so grepping for it returned 0 on a perfect assembly. "Final assembly:" is
# main.py:261, the last line of JobFinalize, and JobFinalize is appended last (main.py:395,
# after JobPolishing), so it is printed only once polishing and scaffolding have finished.
# A plausible sentinel that lives on a code path your invocation skips looks verified and is not.
DONE=$(grep -c 'INFO: Final assembly:' flye.log || true)
N=$(grep -c '^>' assembly.fasta)
TOT=$(awk '!/^>/{t+=length($0)} END{printf "%.0f", t}' assembly.fasta)
BIG=$(awk '/^>/{if(s>m)m=s; s=0; next}{s+=length($0)} END{if(s>m)m=s; printf "%.0f", m}' assembly.fasta)
# assembly_info.txt: #seq_name length cov. circ. repeat mult. alt_group graph_path
CIRC=$(awk 'NR>1 && $4=="Y"' assembly_info.txt | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
BIGCOV=$(awk 'NR>1{if($2>m){m=$2; c=$3}} END{print c}' assembly_info.txt)
BIGCIRC=$(awk 'NR>1{if($2>m){m=$2; c=$4}} END{print c}' assembly_info.txt)

{
  echo "flye_done            $DONE   want 1   [completion sentinel: INFO: Final assembly:]"
  echo "total_length         $TOT   want 4400000..5400000 (E. coli is ~4.6 Mb)"
  echo "largest_contig       $BIG   want >= 4000000 (a chromosome, not fragments)"
  echo "largest_is_circular  $BIGCIRC   want Y (a closed bacterial chromosome)"
  echo "largest_contig_cov   ${BIGCOV}x"
  echo "contigs              $N   (observation: thread count moves this)"
  echo "circular_contigs     $CIRC   (observation)"
  echo "wall_s               $WALL"
  echo "tmpfs_peak_used_mb   $PEAK"
  echo "host_mem_peak_mb     $RSS   <- what actually sizes the box"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
test "$DONE" -ge 1
awk -v t="$TOT" 'BEGIN{exit !(t>=4400000 && t<=5400000)}'
awk -v b="$BIG" 'BEGIN{exit !(b>=4000000)}'
test "$BIGCIRC" = 'Y'
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
